chunks: Sahl narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Madainy, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about singing/music, and I was present, so he said: 'Do not enter houses in which Allah is turned away from its inhabitants.'

key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: Its inhabitants, referring to the people of the house where the singing takes place.
key_terms.الْغِنَاءِ: Singing or music, specifically melodic vocalization often associated with entertainment or leisure.
key_terms.مُعْرِضٌ: Turned away or averted, referring to Allah's turning away His attention or blessings.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on singing (al-ghina') according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the specific art of *al-ghina'* (melodic singing) to spiritual alienation by citing the Quranic principle that Allah turns away from those who engage in it. This ruling, recorded by Sahl from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Madani, underscores the Shia scholarly view that *al-ghina'* is not merely entertainment but a cause of divine displeasure, effectively barring the practitioner from the spiritual presence of God.
